newsitem.title: USA: Orange County transcripts must remain sealed - D.A.
newsitem.headline: Orange County transcripts must remain sealed - D.A.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., district attorney's office has determined that there is no legal way for it to release transcripts from the grand jury's bankruptcy-related probe of Merrill Lynch & Co, officials said on Friday.

County prosecutors reviewed the case law and related statutes, and reached the "preliminary determination that the transcripts cannot be released lawfully" because there was no indictment from the grand jury, said Mark Sevigny, deputy Orange County district attorney.
"When there's no indictment, the grand jury testimony has to be sealed," he said.

A hearing has been set for July 30 in Orange County Superior Court to debate the issue. Local news organizations were expected to ask the district attorney's office to make the grand jury transcripts public.

The southern California county shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it filed for bankruptcy after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. Orange County emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
In June, Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $30 million to settle a 2-1/2 year investigation by the Orange County district attorney's office of the bankruptcy crisis.

The record settlement marked the end of the district attorney's probe of the powerful New York brokerage firm and other Wall Street bond houses, and ensured Merrill Lynch and its employees would not face criminal charges.
